title: Home Delivered Meals for Seniors: What Your Options Are
summary: Explore home delivered meals for seniors, from Meals on Wheels and prepared meals to restaurant and grocery delivery, and find the option that fits your needs.
body_markdown:
‍ **Home delivered meals for seniors come from a handful of places: local programs like Meals on Wheels, companies that ship ready-made meals, restaurant delivery, and grocery delivery if you still enjoy cooking. The right fit depends on your budget, your diet, how often you need meals, and whether you'd rather order by phone or by app.**


## **Key Takeaways**


- Meals on Wheels and other local senior nutrition programs serve adults 60 and older, and meals may be free or on a sliding scale, but eligibility varies and many areas have waitlists.
- Prepared-meal companies ship ready-made meals you reheat, which suits a steady weekly routine.
- Restaurant delivery can bring you a hot meal the same day, though many services take orders through an app.
- You don't have to pick just one. You can mix a program meal on weekdays with a favorite restaurant order on the weekend.


Cooking every day gets harder for all kinds of reasons. Maybe your knee complains after twenty minutes at the stove, or you're home from a hospital stay. Maybe the numbers on the oven dial are harder to read.


Or maybe you're simply cooking for one after decades of cooking for a whole family. None of that means giving up good food. It means getting help with the part that has become hard, and keeping control of the rest.


## **What are the options for home delivered meals?**


Senior meal delivery isn't one service. It's a handful of different ones, and each works best for a different situation. Here's how they compare.

## **Who qualifies for Meals on Wheels?**


According to[Meals on Wheels America](https://www.mealsonwheelsamerica.org/find-meals-and-services/) , adults 60 and older with mobility challenges that make it hard to shop for food, prepare meals, or socialize are eligible. The exact rules vary by area and provider, so your local program has the final say.


Cost varies the same way. Meals may be free, have a suggested donation, or be paid for on a sliding scale based on location, income, and need.


Demand is the catch. "Every year, Meals on Wheels serves over 2 million seniors, but that's only a fraction of those waiting for help," the organization says, and it describes a national crisis of waitlists. If a local program sounds right for you, call sooner rather than later and ask how long the wait is.


Many programs offer more than the meal itself. Depending on the provider, services may include community dining, nutrition counseling, pet food assistance, transportation, and social connection programs. If you live alone, the person at the door can matter as much as what's in the container.


To find a program near you, enter your zip code on the Meals on Wheels America website. You can also call the[Eldercare Locator](https://eldercare.acl.gov/) at 1-800-677-1116, a public service of the Administration for Community Living that connects older adults and their families with local services.


## **How do prepared meal delivery services work?**


Prepared food delivery for seniors works like this: a company cooks the meals and ships them to your door, usually chilled or frozen, ready to reheat. They suit you if you like a freezer stocked for the week and don't mind the microwave doing the work.


These companies vary a lot, so ask a few questions before you sign up:


- **Does the menu fit your diet?** Lower sodium, softer textures, or smaller portions, for example.
- **Is it a subscription?** If so, can you pause or skip a week easily?
- **Can you order by phone?** Some companies are online only.
- **How much freezer space will a week of meals take?**


If your doctor has recommended a specific diet, ask them or a registered dietitian which kind of meal service fits best. The label on the box isn't the same as advice from someone who knows your health.


## **What if you'd rather keep cooking?**


For plenty of older adults, cooking isn't the problem. The shopping is. Carrying heavy bags, standing in checkout lines, and driving to the store in bad weather can wear you out before you've even turned on the stove.


Grocery delivery handles that part.[GoGo Delivery](https://www.gogograndparent.com/services/groceries-for-seniors) handles groceries by phone: you call with what you need, from fresh produce to pantry staples, and a personal shopper places the order. No app, no website.


You might also want help with the cooking itself, whether that's a few dishes prepped for the week or a meal made together. The guide to[what a personal chef for seniors actually does](https://www.gogograndparent.com/blog/meal-prep-and-cooking-help-for-seniors) walks through what that help can look like.


## **How do you choose the right meal delivery option?**


There's no single best meal delivery service for seniors. It depends on what your week actually looks like. These questions narrow it down:


1. **How many meals a week do you need help with?** One or two is a different problem from every lunch and dinner.
2. **Do you follow a special diet?** If so, start with a local program or a company whose menus match it.
3. **Phone or app?** Be honest about which one feels comfortable. The best service is the one you'll actually use.
4. **Hot meal now, or a stocked freezer?** Restaurant delivery covers the first. Prepared meals cover the second.
5. **Would a friendly face at the door help?** Local programs often bring that along with the meal.


You can combine options: groceries for dishes you enjoy making and restaurant delivery on days you'd rather skip cooking.


## **How can family help set up meal delivery from far away?**


Meal delivery for seniors is one of the easier things a family member can help with from another city. A few ways to do it:


- **Make the first call together.** Calling a local program or meal company on speakerphone means you both hear the details, and nobody has to remember them alone.
- **Write the numbers down.** Put the local program's number and any meal service number on the fridge, in large print.
- **Get added to the account.** With GoGoGrandparent, a family member who has been added to the account as someone who can make requests can call and arrange orders too.
- **Check in on how it's going.** A simple "what did you have for dinner this week?" tells you whether the plan is actually working, without turning it into an inspection.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Who qualifies for home delivered meals?**


It depends on the program. Meals on Wheels generally serves adults 60 and older who have trouble shopping, cooking, or getting out, and prepared-meal companies and restaurant delivery are open to anyone.


### **Are home delivered meals for seniors free?**


Sometimes. Meals on Wheels may offer free meals, request a donation, or use a sliding scale. Commercial services charge for meals, sometimes through a subscription.


### **Can I order meal delivery without a smartphone?**


Yes. Local programs are usually arranged by phone, and GoGoGrandparent takes restaurant meal orders at1 (855) 464-6872 , press 7.


### **What if I'm on a special diet?**


Ask your doctor or a registered dietitian which type of meal service fits, then look for a program or company whose menus match.
